extracted.intended_audience: NIH study section chairs, NIH peer reviewers, and NIH grant applicants interested in peer review process
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and critique about the study-section Chair's end-of-discussion summary in NIH peer review — what the Chair summary is supposed to do, common problems, and how it can bias outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brief summary focusing on major strengths and weaknesses
rubrics_metrics.description: At the end of the discussion of your NIH grant proposal in a study section meeting, the Chair of the panel is supposed to summarize the discussion in brief comments. Slide 12 says the purpose is to focus the panel’s attention on the set of major strengths and weaknesses. It is not a listing of every point and it is supposed to overview the score driving comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep the summary short and high-level; do not attempt to catalogue all points from discussion. Emphasize the handful of strengths/weaknesses that are most likely to drive scoring (the 'score-driving' comments).

rubrics_metrics.name: Note areas of consensus and difference
rubrics_metrics.description: The Chair is instructed to note areas of consensus and difference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly state where the panel agrees and where opinions diverge so voters understand the distribution of views rather than a single interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Must not substitute for reviewers paying attention
rubrics_metrics.description: This slide says this is not supposed to substitute for reviewer’s paying attention to the ongoing discussion from the assigned reviewers and other panel members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The summary is an aid, not a replacement; panel members should listen during the discussion and form their own views rather than rely on the Chair summary as the authoritative account.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid introducing points that were not discussed
rubrics_metrics.description: Chairs sometimes 'mention stuff that was in the written critiques but never made it to discussion.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not present as discussion outcomes items that were only in written critiques and were not actually discussed in the meeting—summaries should reflect what was said during the discussion, not add new issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid biasing the vote; be fair and neutral
rubrics_metrics.description: The effect of the Chair summary... is to put a thumb of bias on the scale of merit evaluation. There is the inevitable recency effect... implicit bias... Their take on this is not the same as everyone’s take... Their take may not even reflect the central tendency of the panel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame comments neutrally, avoid strong evaluative language that pushes voters, and be explicit when a point reflects the Chair's impression rather than panel consensus. Strive for balanced wording so the summary does not steer voting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be mindful of recency and authority effects
rubrics_metrics.description: There is the inevitable recency effect, since it comes in close proximity to voting. There is the inevitable implicit bias... The authority of the Chair... influences the panel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that timing and the Chair's authority can disproportionately influence voting; mitigate by being concise, avoiding definitive statements about how members should vote, and by clearly identifying contested points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on score-driving points
rubrics_metrics.description: The Chair is supposed to 'overview the score driving comments.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify which aspects of the discussion are most likely to change or determine the numerical scores and explain why, rather than reciting peripheral observations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not oversell weaknesses or strengths; accurately reflect discussion balance
rubrics_metrics.description: Sometimes Chairs 'try to over sell weaknesses or strengths' and 'their perception of consensus differs' from others' experiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid exaggeration. If the panel was split or ambivalent, state that rather than presenting a lopsided narrative. If you sense an attempt to 'oversell' a position, correct the framing to reflect the actual balance of views.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge practical difficulty and acceptable preparatory work
rubrics_metrics.description: The author notes 'this is a hard job, the Chair summary. The pace of discussion is fast, and the summary is only part of the duties of the Chair. It is perfectly understandable that they would write themselves some notes based on the written critiques before the discussion occurs.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is reasonable for Chairs to prepare notes in advance to manage the fast pace, but they should ensure the final summary is updated to reflect the live discussion and not merely read a pre-prepared account that misstates what actually occurred.
